cards.headline: Port St. Lucie woman charged in alleged $57 million IRS refund fraud scheme
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie woman is among seven people charged in an alleged tax refund fraud scheme that sought more than $57 million from the IRS. Federal prosecutors say the group received more than $8 million in taxpayer money through false returns.
cards.body:
Sherita Chandler of Port St. Lucie is among seven people charged in an alleged tax refund fraud scheme that sought more than $57 million from the IRS, according to the U.S. Justice Department. A superseding indictment unsealed Wednesday charges Chandler, along with defendants from Idaho, Illinois, California and Georgia, with conspiracy to commit wire fraud, making false claims and money laundering.

Federal prosecutors allege the group worked from 2023 through 2024 to prepare and submit false individual and trust tax returns, along with more than 100 fictitious financial instruments, to claim refunds from the IRS. The defendants allegedly sought more than $57 million in refunds and received more than $8 million in taxpayer money. Andrea and Kent Shannon of Kuna, Idaho, also face additional allegations involving wire fraud, false claims and money laundering, including claims that they bought luxury vehicles with fraudulently obtained refunds.

Chandler, the Shannons, and Monika Skinger of Chicago had previously been charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud. The investigation is being handled by IRS Criminal Investigation. A conspiracy to commit wire fraud charge carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison. An indictment is an allegation, and all defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.

cards.headline: Four Fort Pierce officers credited with pulling woman from South Causeway Bridge railing
cards.teaser: Four Fort Pierce police officers are being credited with saving a woman experiencing a mental health crisis on the South Causeway Bridge. The officers pulled her from the bridge railing and ensured she received appropriate care.
cards.body:
Four officers with the Fort Pierce Police Department saved a woman who was having a mental health crisis on the South Causeway Bridge on Wednesday. The woman was sitting on the outer railing of the bridge facing the water when officers arrived.

Two officers kept the woman focused while assessing the situation. The other two officers then pulled her from the railing and back to safety when immediate action became necessary.

All four officers worked together to protect the woman from further harm and ensure she received appropriate care. The Fort Pierce Police Department said in a Facebook post that their teamwork, compassion, and decisive action directly saved a life and exemplified their commitment to protecting the community.

hero.headline: Driver airlifted to trauma center after rollover crash into palm tree on I-95 in Palm City
hero.body:
A driver involved in a single-car rollover crash Friday night was flown to the hospital with traumatic injuries by LifeStar after crashing into a palm tree on Interstate 95 southbound in Palm City, Martin County Fire Rescue said. The crash occurred just after 6:15 p.m. near the High Meadows exit at Mile Marker 102, near Florida's Turnpike. MCFR's special operations team worked to extricate the driver from the car, which had rolled over onto its side.

No other vehicles were involved in the collision. The Martin County Sheriff's Office and Florida Highway Patrol also responded to the scene. MCFR crews who responded included Heavy Rescue 23, LifeStar, Alert 1, Rescue 211, Rescue 231, Engine 21, Engine 22, EMS 2, and Battalion 2 3, according to a Facebook post by the agency.

All lanes of Interstate 95 southbound have been reopened. The nearest trauma center is HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in Fort Pierce, which is 26 miles north. The closest Level 1 trauma center is St. Mary's Medical Center in West Palm Beach, about 38 miles south.

Martin County Fire Rescue praised the C-Shift crews for their rescue work at the scene. The agency posted updates about the crash and the multi-agency response on Facebook Friday night.

hero.headline: Vero Beach woman arrested on capital sexual battery charges after multi-state child abuse investigation
hero.body:
Lisette Zamarripa, 28, of Vero Beach was arrested Sept. 3 by the Indian River County Sheriff's Office on two counts of sexual battery and one count of electronic transmission of child sexual abuse material following an Internet Crimes Against Children investigation that began in Michigan. The Florida Department of Children and Families took custody of her two biological children, a 1-year-old girl and a 2-year-old boy. Prosecutors intended to seek a grand jury indictment on two counts of capital sexual battery because of the children's ages, according to an arrest affidavit. She is being held without bond on the two sexual battery charges and with bond set at $500,000, cash or surety, on the electronic transmission charge.

Michigan State Police received a National Center for Missing and Exploited Children cybertip involving alleged child sexual abuse material associated with a Kik account. Investigators obtained a search warrant for the account and found images and videos allegedly showing an adult woman engaging in sexual acts with the two children. Michigan investigators identified the woman as Zamarripa after comparing material from the account with her Facebook profile, the affidavit states. Michigan investigators also served a search warrant on Zamarripa's boyfriend, Kenneth Conkle, where he admitted to directing and recording the abuse and confessed to separately abusing his own 1-year-old daughter.

Indian River County deputies went to Zamarripa's Vero Beach home after investigators believed the children could be in immediate danger. A family member confirmed Zamarripa was inside with her two children, according to the affidavit. Deputies said Zamarripa came outside with the children and was separated from them. After being advised of her rights, she allegedly admitted that she committed sexual acts involving both children during a FaceTime call with their biological father, who lives in Michigan. The affidavit says Zamarripa told detectives the acts had been discussed with the father beforehand and that she livestreamed at least one incident for him to view.

The children's biological father faces charges in Michigan including child sexual battery, four counts of production of aggravated child sexual abuse material, and five counts of using a computer to commit a crime. Florida charges against Conkle are pending. Deputies seized Zamarripa's cellphone, which she allegedly said was used to record the material. Zamarripa's arraignment is scheduled for 9 a.m.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce Central High School evacuated after bomb threat; no device found
cards.teaser: Fort Pierce Central High School was evacuated Friday afternoon following a bomb threat. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Team gave the all clear at around 3 p.m. after finding no devices.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce Central High School was evacuated Friday afternoon after a bomb threat was reported, and the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Team gave the all clear at around 3 p.m. following comprehensive sweeps that located no devices. The area around the school was secured and evacuated at around 1 p.m. while personnel conducted their assessment, evaluation and investigation. Students were released from school and after school activities resumed as planned, according to Lydia Martin of St. Lucie County Public Schools.

Parents rushed to the school to pick up their children following the evacuation. Angela Jones, who picked up her son, said her heart was shaking and she was nervous. Cleveland Jamison Jr., a freshman at Fort Pierce Central High School, said he was inside the school when the threat was made and everybody got scared and ran into the room.

St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said his office takes all threats seriously but noted the real-world consequences of false alarms. "We take everything serious, but, you know, those types of pranks cost the communities a lot of money and obviously school time when stuff like that happens," Del Toro said. "When those happen, we do follow do a thorough follow-up investigation, and if we can arrest somebody in those types of calls, we make sure we do that."

Brandon Isaiah Martin, 24, was arrested Sept. 2 on an outstanding warrant charging him with aggravated battery with a deadly weapon. The warrant identifies a motor vehicle as the alleged weapon. The charge stems from an April 28, 2025, incident on 26th Court Southwest in Vero Beach, court records show. As the woman was placing one of the children into another vehicle, Martin allegedly drove a silver Kia Soul toward her and struck her, causing her to land on the hood, deputies wrote. A witness told deputies she saw Martin drive toward the woman, strike her and continue down the street with the woman still on the hood. Deputies documented abrasions to the woman’s knees, records show. The order also prohibits him from contacting the woman and requires him to stay specified distances away from her, her home, workplace and vehicle. Deputies served Martin with the warrant at a Vero Beach address on Sept. Jail records show he later posted bond.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie woman charged in superseding indictment alleging $57M IRS refund fraud scheme
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie woman is among seven people named in a superseding federal indictment charging them with conspiracy to commit wire fraud, making false claims and money laundering in an alleged tax refund fraud scheme that sought more than $57 million from the IRS.
cards.body:
A superseding indictment unsealed Wednesday charges Sherita Chandler of Port St. Lucie and six other defendants with conspiracy to commit wire fraud, making false claims and money laundering in an alleged tax refund fraud scheme that sought more than $57 million from the IRS and received more than $8 million in taxpayer money, according to the U.S. Justice Department. Federal prosecutors allege the group worked from 2023 through 2024 to prepare and submit false individual and trust tax returns, along with more than 100 fictitious financial instruments, to claim refunds from the IRS.

Chandler, Andrea and Kent Shannon of Kuna, Idaho, and Monika Skinger of Chicago had previously been charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud. The Shannons also face additional allegations involving wire fraud, false claims and money laundering, including claims that they bought luxury vehicles with fraudulently obtained refunds. The defendants also include people from California and Georgia.

The investigation is being handled by IRS Criminal Investigation. A conspiracy to commit wire fraud charge carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison. An indictment is an allegation, and all defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.

hero.headline: Vero Beach mother arrested on capital sexual battery charges after ICAC probe traced livestreamed abuse of two toddlers
hero.body:
A Vero Beach woman faces two counts of capital sexual battery after an Internet Crimes Against Children investigation in Michigan traced livestreamed abuse of her two toddlers to her Indian River County home, according to an arrest affidavit. Lisette Zamarripa, 28, was arrested Sept. 3 by the Indian River County Sheriff's Office and is being held without bond on the sexual battery charges. Prosecutors intend to seek a grand jury indictment on two counts of capital sexual battery because the victims, a 1-year-old girl and a 2-year-old boy, are both under age 3. The Department of Children and Families took custody of the children.

Michigan State Police received a National Center for Missing and Exploited Children cybertip involving alleged child sexual abuse material associated with a Kik account. Investigators obtained a search warrant for the account and found images and videos allegedly showing an adult woman engaging in sexual acts with the two children, both Zamarripa's biological children, according to the affidavit. Michigan investigators identified Zamarripa after comparing material from the account with her Facebook profile. Michigan investigators also served a search warrant on Zamarripa's boyfriend, Kenneth Conkle, where he admitted to directing and recording the abuse and confessed to separately abusing his own 1-year-old daughter.

Indian River County deputies went to Zamarripa's Vero Beach home after investigators believed the children could be in immediate danger. A family member confirmed Zamarripa was inside with her two children, and deputies said Zamarripa came outside with the children and was separated from them. After being advised of her rights, she allegedly admitted that she committed sexual acts involving both children during a FaceTime call with their biological father, who lives in Michigan. The affidavit says Zamarripa told detectives the acts had been discussed with the father beforehand and that she livestreamed at least one incident for him to view.

The biological father faces charges in Michigan including child sexual battery, four counts of production of aggravated child sexual abuse material, and five counts of using a computer to commit a crime. Florida charges against Conkle are pending. Zamarripa is also charged with one count of electronic transmission of child sexual abuse material, with bond set at $500,000, cash or surety, on that charge. Deputies seized Zamarripa's cellphone, which she allegedly said was used to record the material. Her arraignment is scheduled for 9 a.m.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce Central High School evacuated after bomb threat, given all clear by sheriff's bomb team
hero.body:
Fort Pierce Central High School was evacuated Friday afternoon after a bomb threat, and the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Team gave the all clear at around 3 p.m. following comprehensive sweeps of the campus. No devices were located, and the scene has been deemed safe, deputies said. The area around the school was secured and evacuated at around 1 p.m. while personnel conducted their assessment, evaluation and investigation, the sheriff's office said.

Lydia Martin of St. Lucie County Public Schools said parents were notified of the threat. A second message was sent to parents confirming the school had been cleared by law enforcement. Students were released from school and after school activities will resume as planned, Martin said.

Parents rushed to the school to pick up their children following the evacuation. Angela Jones, who was there to pick up her son, said the timing made the situation even more unsettling. "My heart was shaking, I was nervous. I can't believe this, on a Friday, too, with a long weekend coming up," she said. "That's my only child. So, you know, I'm just like, okay, what do I do, you know? Yeah, very scary." Cleveland Jamison Jr., a freshman at Fort Pierce Central High School, said he was inside the school when the threat was made. "Everybody got scared, everybody ran into the room and all the kids were going crazy—people were calling their moms," he said.

St. Lucie County Sheriff Del Toro said his office takes all threats seriously, but noted the real-world consequences of false alarms. "We take everything serious, but, you know, those types of pranks cost the communities a lot of money and obviously school time when stuff like that happens," he said. "When those happen, we do follow do a thorough follow-up investigation, and if we can arrest somebody in those types of calls, we make sure we do that." During the incident, the sheriff's office asked the public to avoid the affected area and follow all instructions from law enforcement and emergency personnel.

hero.headline: Rollover crash on I-95 southbound in Palm City leaves driver with traumatic injuries, requiring airlift
hero.body:
A driver with traumatic injuries was airlifted by LifeStar following a violent rollover crash on I-95 southbound in Palm City, according to Martin County Fire Rescue. The crash occurred just after 6:15 p.m. on Friday near the High Meadows exit.

A small sedan rolled over onto its side and crashed into a palm tree. Martin County Fire Rescue's special operations team quickly worked to extract the driver from the vehicle. The driver was then airlifted by LifeStar for treatment of traumatic injuries.

No other vehicles were involved in the crash, according to Martin County Fire Rescue. The incident shut down lanes of I-95 southbound while emergency crews worked at the scene and extracted the trapped driver.

All lanes of I-95 southbound have since reopened. Martin County Fire Rescue responded to the single-vehicle rollover crash that left the sedan on its side against a palm tree near the High Meadows exit in Palm City.

lead_independence.headline: First Border Collies adopted after Palm City hoarding rescue, Humane Society says
lead_independence.lead: The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast has begun placing Border Collies rescued from a Palm City hoarding case into new homes, marking a major milestone in the dogs' recovery less than a month after Martin County deputies and Animal Services removed 36 Border Collies from a home on Southwest Alligator Street in Palm City. The shelter said it has slowly started facilitating adoptions and shared photos from one of the first successful placements. Shelter staff will stay in regular contact with adopters, conduct follow-up checks and provide support during the transition, and training classes will be available for dogs needing extra attention or help adjusting to life in a home.

hero.headline: Vero Beach woman held without bond after Michigan ICAC investigation leads to arrest for livestreamed sexual abuse of two toddlers
hero.body:
A Vero Beach woman is being held without bond on two sexual battery charges after an Internet Crimes Against Children investigation in Michigan led deputies to her Indian River County home. Lisette Zamarripa, 28, was arrested Sept. 3 by the Indian River County Sheriff's Office and charged with two counts of sexual battery and one count of electronic transmission of child sexual abuse material. Prosecutors intend to seek a grand jury indictment on two counts of capital sexual battery because of the children's ages, according to an arrest affidavit. Bond was set at $500,000 on the electronic transmission charge.

Michigan State Police received a National Center for Missing and Exploited Children cybertip involving alleged child sexual abuse material associated with a Kik account. Investigators obtained a search warrant for the account and found images and videos allegedly showing an adult woman engaging in sexual acts with two children, a 1-year-old girl and a 2-year-old boy, both her biological children. Michigan investigators identified the woman as Zamarripa after comparing material from the account with her Facebook profile, the affidavit states. The Department of Children and Families took custody of the children.

Indian River County deputies went to Zamarripa's Vero Beach home after investigators believed the children could be in immediate danger. A family member confirmed Zamarripa was inside with her two children. Deputies said Zamarripa came outside with the children and was separated from them. After being advised of her rights, she allegedly admitted that she committed sexual acts involving both children during a FaceTime call with their biological father, who lives in Michigan. The affidavit says Zamarripa told detectives the acts had been discussed with the father beforehand and that she livestreamed at least one incident for him to view.

Michigan investigators also served a search warrant on Zamarripa's boyfriend, Kenneth Conkle, where he admitted to directing and recording the abuse. He confessed to separately abusing his own 1-year-old daughter. The children's biological father faces charges in Michigan including child sexual battery, four counts of production of aggravated child sexual abuse material, and five counts of using a computer to commit a crime. Florida charges against Conkle are pending. Deputies seized Zamarripa's cellphone, which she allegedly said was used to record the material. Zamarripa's arraignment is scheduled for 9 a.m.

cards.headline: Vero Beach police charge Peter Ruma with eight counts for AI-generated sexual deepfakes, warn of additional victims
cards.teaser: Vero Beach police arrested a 37-year-old man on eight criminal charges for using artificial intelligence to create and distribute sexually explicit altered images of women without their consent. Detectives believe additional victims exist and urge anyone with information to come forward.
cards.body:
Vero Beach police arrested Peter Solomon Ruma, 37, on eight criminal charges after investigators determined he used artificial intelligence to create and distribute sexually explicit altered images of women without their consent. The charges include three counts of creation of an altered sexual depiction of an identifiable person, three counts of promotion of an altered sexual depiction of an identifiable person, one count of sexual cyberharassment, and one count of stalking. Detectives executed search warrants on Ruma's residence and electronic devices, and a forensic examination recovered evidence investigators believe is associated with the creation and distribution of altered sexual images.

The current charges stem from incidents between June and August 2026 and relate to one female victim. Detectives identified several additional females believed to have been victimized through similar conduct and have information indicating Ruma may have engaged in this type of conduct for several years. Vero Beach Police Chief David Curry warned that Ruma is a driver for Uber Eats and Lyft and suggested that anyone who has had concerning interactions with Ruma come forward. Ruma is being held at the Indian River County Sheriff's Office on a $1 million bond, and the investigation remains ongoing with additional charges possible as additional victims or evidence are identified.

Anyone who believes they may have been victimized by Ruma, or who has received, viewed, or has information regarding altered or sexually explicit images allegedly created or distributed by Ruma, is encouraged to contact Detective Matakaetis of the Vero Beach Police Department at 772-978-4665. Those wishing to remain anonymous can contact Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 800-273-8477.

cards.headline: Child safety experts warn Indian River County residents of AI image risks after Vero Beach arrest
cards.teaser: Following the arrest of a Vero Beach man accused of using artificial intelligence to turn social media photos into pornography, child safety experts are urging Indian River County residents to reconsider what they post online.
cards.body:
Following the arrest of Peter Ruma, a Vero Beach man accused of using artificial intelligence to turn social media photos into pornography, child safety experts are warning Indian River County residents about the growing threat of AI-manipulated images. Greg Schiller, CEO of the Boca Raton-based nonprofit Child Rescue Coalition, said this type of activity is becoming increasingly common and that a photo posted on social media today could be altered into pornography by tomorrow. While Ruma's case does not involve children, Schiller said the accusations serve as a reminder that predators can use a simple photo of a child to create harmful content.

Schiller said the increased number of cyber tips related to AI-generated child sexual abuse material has gone through the roof. He advised keeping social media settings private and limiting who can see posts, though he emphasized that nothing is truly safe on the internet. The easiest way to protect yourself and your family is to stop posting on social media, Schiller said, but for those who continue posting, thinking before sharing images is critical.

Ruma is currently charged with altering photos of one woman, but police believe there may be more victims and additional charges could follow. The Child Rescue Coalition provides technology to help law enforcement track down child sex predators worldwide.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce Central High evacuated after bomb threat; deputies give all-clear
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office gave the all-clear Friday after a bomb threat forced the evacuation of Fort Pierce Central High School at midday. Deputies conducted an extensive sweep of the campus and found no devices, declaring the scene safe. The threat came in at 12:31 p.m., prompting authorities to evacuate all students from the building. The campus underwent a modified dismissal as law enforcement searched the school.

St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said deputies decided to evacuate all students due to the nature of the call. The sheriff's office said deputies and emergency personnel assessed the situation, secured the area and determined the appropriate response. Specialized resources were deployed to assist with the evaluation and investigation.

The sheriff's office worked alongside its bomb squad and the Fort Pierce Police Department to investigate the threat. Authorities swept the entire campus during the disruption to the school day. The investigation remained active as deputies worked to determine the source and credibility of the threat.

The all-clear came after the extensive search confirmed no suspicious devices were located on campus. The sheriff's office said the scene was deemed safe following the sweep. Fort Pierce Central High School students were released under the modified dismissal procedure as authorities completed their security protocols.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce police search for three masked suspects after fatal shooting
cards.teaser: A man died after being shot multiple times in Fort Pierce following a verbal altercation. Three masked males fled the scene and remain at large.
cards.body:
A man died after being shot multiple times in Fort Pierce following a verbal altercation, and police continue searching for three masked suspects who fled the area. Officers located the man suffering from multiple gunshot wounds in September and transported him to a local hospital, where he later died. Witnesses reported seeing three masked males run away from the area following the shooting.

According to the preliminary investigation, the victim became involved in a verbal altercation with several individuals before shots were fired. A firearm was located near the victim, and multiple shell casings were recovered from the scene.

Detectives are continuing to gather evidence and interview witnesses as they work to determine the circumstances surrounding the shooting. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at www.tcwatch.org.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce seeks resident input on 2041 strategic plan through Oct. 15 survey and online idea wall
cards.teaser: The city of Fort Pierce is asking residents to help shape its Fort Pierce 2041 strategic plan through an online survey and idea wall. The public engagement platform remains open through Oct. 15.
cards.body:
The city of Fort Pierce is asking residents to help shape its Fort Pierce 2041 strategic plan through an online survey and idea wall. The public engagement platform remains open through Oct. 15. The initiative, called Fort Pierce 2041: One Vision, One Fort Pierce, will establish the city's mission, vision, priorities, goals, and objectives while creating strategies to guide city priorities, investments, services, and decision-making through 2041.

Residents can participate through a community survey that takes approximately 10 minutes to complete, where they can share perspectives on Fort Pierce today and identify priorities for the years ahead. The online platform also features an ideas wall where community members can submit ideas, aspirations, and recommendations for the future of Fort Pierce and explore suggestions shared by others.

Feedback gathered throughout the process will help identify priorities, establish goals, and develop strategies that reflect the community's needs and aspirations. The Fort Pierce Strategic Plan engagement page is available online for residents who live, work, and do business in Fort Pierce.

hero.headline: Florida drivers face record-high Labor Day gas prices as Strait of Hormuz tensions drive fuel costs up
hero.body:
Florida drivers heading out for the Labor Day weekend will face the highest gas prices on record for the holiday, according to AAA. Gas prices are running nearly a dollar higher than this time last year. Martin and Indian River counties are seeing prices at $3.94 per gallon, St. Lucie County at $3.95, and Palm Beach County at $4.10. AAA attributes the record-breaking prices to tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, which have pushed the price of crude oil higher.

AAA says this could be the most expensive Labor Day on record at the pump. Diesel prices are also at a record high. At the West Palm Beach Service Plaza on the Turnpike, drivers said they are feeling the impact.

Eric Perry, of Port St. Lucie, said he has been watching prices climb. "Definitely noticed they've been going up a little bit. It is unfortunate, but it is what it is, I guess," Perry said. Guy Moran, who was heading to the Florida Keys, said prices are noticeably higher. "Slightly higher prices than normal, I'd say," Moran said. Moran said his group found a way to manage the expense. "We're splitting the costs, so one person pays for the Airbnb, one person for the boat, one for gas, so split it that way," Moran said.

AAA says roads will be busiest between noon and 8 p.m. The best times to travel, both heading to a destination and returning home, are Friday and Monday before noon.

hero.headline: Vero Beach mother, Michigan boyfriend arrested after ICAC investigation into livestreamed child sex abuse
hero.body:
A 28-year-old Vero Beach woman and her 38-year-old boyfriend in Michigan are facing child sex abuse charges following a joint Internet Crimes Against Children investigation that began with a cybertip and led to arrests in both states within hours, the Indian River County Sheriff's Office and Van Buren County Sheriff's Office said Friday. The investigation began after law enforcement received a cybertip from the National Center for Missing Exploited Children regarding suspected child sexual abuse material transmitted through the online messaging platform Kik. Investigators obtained legal process for associated online accounts and recovered images, videos and communications that identified an adult female in Florida and an adult male in Michigan as persons of interest.

On Thursday, Indian River County Sheriff's Office internet crimes against children detectives were contacted by the Michigan State Police after investigators there found images and videos on a Kik account showing a woman sexually abusing two young children. Detectives identified the woman as Lisette Zamarripa and responded to her home, where they located and safely removed the two victims, a 1-year-old girl and a 2-year-old boy, both her biological children. Zamarripa admitted to sexually abusing the children and recording it during a video call at the request of her boyfriend, Kenneth Conkle, who was watching from Michigan, the sheriff's office said. She was located and arrested roughly 2.5 hours after detectives received the initial tip and charged with two counts of sexual battery and transmission of child sexual abuse material. The Department of Children and Families took custody of the children.

The Van Buren County Sheriff's Office served a search warrant at Conkle's home, where he admitted to directing and recording the abuse. He confessed to separately abusing his own 1-year-old daughter. Because information indicated firearms were present at the residence, the search warrant was treated as a high-risk operation. During the search, detectives assigned to the Van Buren County Sheriff's Office Computer Crimes Unit seized a cellular telephone, two computers, and a tablet believed to contain evidence of child sexual abuse material. Conkle faces charges including first-degree criminal sexual conduct and multiple counts related to the manufacture of aggravated child sexually abusive material.

Zamarripa is being held in the Indian River County jail on no bond with arraignment set for October. Conkle is in the Van Buren County jail on $2 million bond with a court date set for September. The seized digital devices will undergo forensic examination for additional evidence, and investigators continue to work with their state and federal ICAC partners. Florida charges against Conkle are pending. Additional charges may be authorized as the investigation and forensic examination of the seized devices continue.

cards.headline: Vero Beach man arrested on eight charges for creating, distributing AI-generated sexual images of women without consent
cards.teaser: Peter Solomon Ruma, 37, faces eight criminal charges after police say he used artificial intelligence to create and distribute sexually explicit altered images of women without their consent. Police believe there may be additional victims who have not yet been identified.
cards.body:
Peter Solomon Ruma, 37, of Vero Beach was arrested on eight criminal charges after police say he used artificial intelligence to create and distribute sexually explicit altered images of women without their consent. Ruma faces three counts of creation of an altered sexual depiction of an identifiable person, three counts of promotion of an altered sexual depiction of an identifiable person, one count of sexual cyberharassment, and one count of stalking. The charges stem from incidents occurring between June and August 2026 and relate to one female victim.

Detectives executed search warrants on Ruma's residence and electronic devices during the investigation. A forensic examination of those devices resulted in the recovery of evidence investigators believe is associated with the creation and distribution of altered sexual images. Photographs obtained from social media and other online sources were used to create some of the altered images, according to police.

During the investigation, detectives identified several additional females believed to have been victimized through similar conduct. Investigators also have information indicating Ruma may have engaged in this type of conduct for several years. Anyone who believes they may have been victimized by Ruma, or who has received, viewed, or has information regarding altered or sexually explicit images allegedly created or distributed by Ruma, is encouraged to contact Detective Matakaetis of the Vero Beach Police Department at (772) 978-4665. Ruma is currently being held at the Indian River County Sheriff's Office on a $1 million bond.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie man arrested on warrant for allegedly hitting mother of his children with car in Vero Beach
cards.teaser: Brandon Isaiah Martin, 24, of Port St. Lucie was arrested on an outstanding warrant charging him with aggravated battery with a deadly weapon after allegedly striking the mother of his children with a Kia Soul and driving with her on the hood in April 2025.
cards.body:
Brandon Isaiah Martin, 24, of Port St. Lucie was arrested Sept. 2 on an outstanding warrant charging him with aggravated battery with a deadly weapon after allegedly striking the mother of his children with a Kia Soul and driving with her on the hood during a custody dispute in Vero Beach, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office. The charge stems from an April 28, 2025, incident on 26th Court Southwest in Vero Beach. A judge approved the warrant May 5, 2025, and set Martin's bond at $50,000.

Deputies said the woman went to the home after a friend told her Martin was there removing property. The woman told deputies Martin was attempting to leave with their two children. The pair had joint custody but no formal custody documentation, according to the probable cause affidavit. As the woman was placing one of the children into another vehicle, Martin allegedly drove a silver Kia Soul toward her and struck her, causing her to land on the hood.

The woman told deputies Martin continued driving with her on the hood for about four or five houses. She said she heard him threaten to kill her, according to the affidavit. The vehicle stopped after Martin's mother, who was in the front passenger seat, put it in neutral. A witness told deputies she saw Martin drive toward the woman, strike her and continue down the street with the woman still on the hood. Deputies served Martin with the warrant at a Vero Beach address on Sept. 2. Jail records show he later posted bond.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce Central High School receives all clear after bomb threat and evacuation
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Team gave the all clear at Fort Pierce Central High School Friday afternoon after a bomb threat forced an evacuation. No devices were located during comprehensive sweeps of the school.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Bomb Team gave the all clear at around 3 p.m. Friday following comprehensive sweeps of Fort Pierce Central High School after a bomb threat forced evacuation of the campus. No devices were located, and the scene has been deemed safe, deputies said. The area around Fort Pierce Central High School was secured and evacuated at around 1 p.m. while personnel conducted their assessment, evaluation and investigation.

Lydia Martin of St. Lucie County Public Schools said parents were notified of the threat. A second message was sent to parents confirming the school had been cleared by law enforcement. Students were released from school and after school activities will resume as planned, Martin said.

During the incident, the sheriff's office asked the public to avoid the affected area and follow all instructions from law enforcement and emergency personnel. Residents were also asked not to approach or handle any suspicious items and to report any additional concerns or suspicious activity by calling 911. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office said in a post on Facebook that its priority is protecting the safety of the public, its personnel, and those in the affected area.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce opens public survey through Oct. 15 to help shape strategic plan through 2041
hero.body:
Fort Pierce has launched the Fort Pierce 2041: One Vision, One Fort Pierce strategic planning process and is inviting residents to help shape city priorities and investments through an online engagement platform open through Oct. 15. The city is developing a new strategic plan that will serve as a roadmap for city priorities, investments, services, and decision-making in the years ahead. The strategic planning process will establish the city's mission, vision, priorities, goals, and objectives while creating actionable strategies to guide the organization.

The city has launched an online public engagement platform where community members can participate in two ways. Residents can complete a community survey that asks them to share perspectives on Fort Pierce today, identify priorities, and provide input on opportunities and areas of focus for the years ahead. The survey takes approximately 10 minutes to complete. Community members can also use an ideas wall to submit ideas, aspirations, and recommendations for the future of Fort Pierce and explore suggestions shared by others.

Community input is a key part of the process. Feedback will help city leadership better understand the issues, opportunities, and priorities that matter most to those who live, work, and do business in Fort Pierce. Feedback gathered throughout the process will help identify priorities, establish goals, and develop strategies that reflect the community's needs and aspirations.

The plan will connect the city's near-term priorities with a broader vision for Fort Pierce through 2041. To participate in the survey or learn more, residents can visit the Fort Pierce Strategic Plan engagement page. The Fort Pierce 2041: One Vision, One Fort Pierce public engagement platform will remain open through Oct. 15.

hero.headline: Boca nonprofit warns Treasure Coast parents after Vero Beach AI pornography arrest
hero.teaser: A Boca Raton child protection organization is urging Treasure Coast parents to reconsider what they post online after a Vero Beach man was accused of using artificial intelligence to turn social media photos into pornography.
hero.body:
A Boca Raton child protection organization is urging Treasure Coast parents to reconsider what they post online after a Vero Beach man was accused of using artificial intelligence to turn social media photos into pornography. Greg Schiller, CEO of the nonprofit Child Rescue Coalition, said the arrest of Peter Ruma serves as a reminder that predators can use a simple photo of a child to create harmful content. The increased number of cyber tips related to AI-generated child sexual abuse material has gone through the roof, Schiller said.

Schiller advised parents to keep social media settings private and limit who can see their posts. The easiest way to protect yourself and your family is to stop posting on social media, he said, though he acknowledged that people who continue posting can maintain as much security as possible through privacy controls. Nothing is truly safe on the internet, Schiller said.

Ruma is currently charged with altering photos of one woman. Police believe there may be more victims and additional charges could follow. The Child Rescue Coalition provides technology to help law enforcement track down child sex predators worldwide.
hero.article_text: A Vero Beach man, Peter Ruma, is accused of using artificial intelligence to turn social media photos into pornography, raising concerns about the dangers of posting images on social media. Greg Schiller, CEO of the Boca Raton-based nonprofit Child Rescue Coalition, said this type of activity is becoming increasingly common. "Everyone's got to be concerned about what people are potentially doing with their images," Schiller said. The Child Rescue Coalition provides technology to help law enforcement track down child sex predators worldwide. While Ruma's case does not involve children, Schiller said the accusations serve as a reminder that predators can use a simple photo of a child to create harmful content. "The increased number of cyber tips that are related to AI-generated child sexual abuse material has gone through the roof," Schiller said. He added that this issue applies to adults as well, warning that a photo posted on social media today could be altered into pornography by tomorrow. "I think people need to be conscious of that, know what's happening, and before they post a picture of their child especially, let's think about the idea that people can now use those images," Schiller said. Schiller said the easiest way to protect yourself and your family is to stop posting on social media. However, he also said there are ways to continue posting while maintaining as much security as possible. Schiller advised keeping social media settings private and limiting who can see your posts. At the same time, he also emphasized that nothing is truly safe on the internet. "I think that's the most important message. Just think before you act on these things and understand that there might be repercussions," Schiller said. As for Ruma, he is currently charged with altering photos of one woman, but police believe there may be more victims and additional charges could follow. cards.body:
Vero Beach police confirmed the arrest of Peter Solomon Ruma, 37, on eight criminal charges after investigators say he used artificial intelligence to create and distribute sexually explicit altered images of women without their consent. Vero Beach Police Chief David Curry warned that additional victims and charges are likely, and urged anyone with information to contact detectives. The charges stem from incidents occurring between June and August 2026 and relate to one female victim, but detectives identified several additional females believed to have been victimized through similar conduct. Investigators have information indicating Ruma may have engaged in this type of conduct for several years.

Ruma faces three counts of creation of an altered sexual depiction of an identifiable person in violation of Florida Statute 836.13(2), three counts of promotion of an altered sexual depiction of an identifiable person in violation of Florida Statute 836.13(4), one count of sexual cyberharassment in violation of Florida Statute 784.049(3)(a), and one count of stalking in violation of Florida Statute 784.048(2). According to investigators, Ruma used AI to create sexually explicit altered images depicting victims without their consent and then distributed or promoted those images. Photographs obtained from social media and other online sources were used to create some of the altered images.

Detectives executed search warrants on Ruma's residence and electronic devices during the investigation. A forensic examination of those devices resulted in the recovery of evidence investigators believe is associated with the creation and distribution of altered sexual images. Detectives believe there may be additional victims who have not yet been identified or who may be unaware that altered sexual images depicting them were created or distributed. Chief Curry also warned that Ruma is a driver for Uber Eats and Lyft and suggested that anyone who has had concerning interactions with Ruma also come forward.

Anyone who believes they may have been victimized by Ruma, or who has received, viewed, or has information regarding altered or sexually explicit images allegedly created or distributed by Ruma, is encouraged to contact Detective Matakaetis of the Vero Beach Police Department at 772-978-4665. Those wishing to remain anonymous can contact Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 800-273-8477 and may be eligible for a cash reward. Ruma is being held at the Indian River County Sheriff's Office on a $1 million bond. The Indian River County Sheriff's Office and the State Attorney's Office assisted throughout the investigation.

hero.headline: Man dies after Fort Pierce shooting, three masked suspects sought
hero.body:
A man died Thursday evening after a shooting in the 100 block of North 16th Street in Fort Pierce that followed a verbal altercation, and police are searching for three masked suspects who fled on foot. The victim suffered multiple gunshot wounds and was transported to Lawnwood Medical Center, where he later died from his injuries. Officers responded to reports of multiple gunshots at around 6 p.m.

According to the preliminary investigation, the victim was involved in a verbal altercation with several individuals before the shooting occurred. Police recovered a firearm near the victim and collected multiple shell casings from the scene.

Witnesses told investigators they saw three masked males flee the area on foot immediately after the shooting.

Fort Pierce Police are asking anyone with information about the incident to contact them at 772-467-6800 or submit an anonymous tip through Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at www.tcwatch.org.

hero.headline: Jensen Beach theater screens Dolly Parton films this weekend to benefit children's literacy
hero.body:
Regal Treasure Coast Mall in Jensen Beach is showing two Dolly Parton films this weekend with all ticket proceeds benefiting her children's literacy nonprofit. Steel Magnolias and The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas will screen through September. Tickets cost $9.25, a reference to Parton's hit song 9 to 5.

Regal Cinemas said 100 percent of the proceeds will benefit Dolly Parton's Imagination Library, which provides free books to young children. Regal Royal Palm Beach is also participating in the limited-run screenings.

Other South Florida theaters showing the tribute films include Regal Broward at 8000 W. 1840 in Plantation, Regal Magnolia Place at 9645 Westview Drive in Coral Springs, Regal Sawgrass at 2600 NW 136th Ave. in Sunrise, Regal Southland Mall at 20505 S. Dixie Highway, Suite 1301, in Miami, and Regal Westfork at 15977 Pines Blvd. in Pembroke Pines.

Tickets can be purchased through the Regal mobile app or at regmovies.com.

cards.headline: Vero Beach police expect more victims, charges in AI sexual image case against Peter Ruma
cards.teaser: Vero Beach police say they believe there are additional victims beyond the initial eight charges filed against a man accused of creating and sharing AI-generated sexually explicit images of women without their consent. Detectives have identified several other women who may have been subjected to similar conduct.
cards.body:
Vero Beach police say they believe there are additional victims and expect more charges against Peter Solomon Ruma, 37, who is accused of creating and sharing AI-generated sexually explicit images of women without their consent. Police Chief David Currey said Thursday that the current eight charges against Ruma involve one adult female victim. Ruma is charged with three counts of creating an altered sexual depiction, three counts of promoting an altered sexual depiction, one count of sexual cyber harassment and one count of cyberstalking. He is being held at the Indian River County Jail on $1 million bond.

Currey said investigators have identified several other women who may have been subjected to similar conduct, some of whom may not know their images were obtained, manipulated or shared. Detectives searched Ruma's home and seized two phones, and a forensic review of the devices produced evidence that advanced the investigation. Police said Ruma allegedly used photographs of real women including images from social media and other publicly available online sources to make the altered sexual images. A person does not have to have sent an intimate photo to be victimized, police said.

Ruma is employed as a Lyft driver and Uber Eats driver. Currey stressed that investigators have not alleged criminal conduct occurred while Ruma was working for either service, but released the information as they seek potential victims or people with concerning interactions involving him. The investigation uncovered complaints and law enforcement contacts involving unwanted communications and similar behavior dating back several years. Anyone who believes they may have been victimized, received altered or sexually explicit images from Ruma, or has information for detectives is asked to contact Vero Beach police Detective Greg Matakaitis at 772-978-4665.

hero.body:

Peter Ruma downloaded pictures from social media and used AI prompts to remove women's clothing, placing them in sexual situations, according to authorities. Police said Ruma then distributed the images without the consent of the individuals depicted.

Authorities said Ruma has been engaging in this activity for several years. Police are warning there could be more victims.

Ruma is currently being held in the Indian River County Jail. Police are expected to provide an update this afternoon.

The arrest comes as law enforcement agencies across the country grapple with the misuse of artificial intelligence technology to create non-consensual sexual imagery. The AI tools allow users to digitally manipulate photographs to remove clothing or place individuals in fabricated sexual scenarios.

cards.headline: Boca Raton nonprofit CEO warns Treasure Coast parents about AI-generated exploitation after Vero Beach arrest
cards.teaser: The CEO of a Boca Raton child-safety nonprofit is using a Vero Beach man's arrest to warn parents about artificial intelligence being used to turn social media photos into pornography. Greg Schiller said the best protection is to stop posting, but offered steps to reduce risk for those who continue sharing images.
cards.body:
Greg Schiller, CEO of the Boca Raton-based nonprofit Child Rescue Coalition, said the arrest of Vero Beach man Peter Ruma for allegedly using artificial intelligence to turn social media photos into pornography should serve as a warning to parents and social media users. Ruma is accused of altering photos of one woman, but police believe there may be more victims and additional charges could follow. Schiller said the increased number of cyber tips related to AI-generated child sexual abuse material has gone through the roof, and predators can use a simple photo of a child to create harmful content.

Schiller said the easiest way to protect yourself and your family is to stop posting on social media. For those who continue posting, he advised keeping social media settings private and limiting who can see posts. He emphasized that nothing is truly safe on the internet and urged people to think before posting photos of their children, knowing that people can now use those images to create altered content. The Child Rescue Coalition provides technology to help law enforcement track down child sex predators worldwide.
cards.article_text: A Vero Beach man, Peter Ruma, is accused of using artificial intelligence to turn social media photos into pornography, raising concerns about the dangers of posting images on social media. Greg Schiller, CEO of the Boca Raton-based nonprofit Child Rescue Coalition, said this type of activity is becoming increasingly common. "Everyone's got to be concerned about what people are potentially doing with their images," Schiller said. The Child Rescue Coalition provides technology to help law enforcement track down child sex predators worldwide. While Ruma's case does not involve children, Schiller said the accusations serve as a reminder that predators can use a simple photo of a child to create harmful content. "The increased number of cyber tips that are related to AI-generated child sexual abuse material has gone through the roof," Schiller said. He added that this issue applies to adults as well, warning that a photo posted on social media today could be altered into pornography by tomorrow. "I think people need to be conscious of that, know what's happening, and before they post a picture of their child especially, let's think about the idea that people can now use those images," Schiller said. Schiller said the easiest way to protect yourself and your family is to stop posting on social media. However, he also said there are ways to continue posting while maintaining as much security as possible. Schiller advised keeping social media settings private and limiting who can see your posts. At the same time, he also emphasized that nothing is truly safe on the internet. "I think that's the most important message. Just think before you act on these things and understand that there might be repercussions," Schiller said. As for Ruma, he is currently charged with altering photos of one woman, but police believe there may be more victims and additional charges could follow. cards.headline: 17-year-old in custody after Indian River County shootout with 15-year-old, weapon recovered
cards.teaser: Deputies have taken a 17-year-old suspect into custody and recovered a short-barreled pistol following a shootout with a 15-year-old in a residential neighborhood. Video evidence confirms the two teens fired at each other in the middle of the street.
cards.body:
Deputies with the Indian River County Sheriff's Office took a 17-year-old suspect into custody Thursday morning and recovered a weapon after investigating a shootout with a 15-year-old in a residential neighborhood Wednesday night. Investigators obtained video showing the two teenagers shooting at each other in the roadway in the 1100 block of 12th Court Southwest around 7:30 p.m., according to Kevin Jaworski with the sheriff's office.

Deputies responded to multiple 911 calls and found bullet casings at the scene. A nearby home and vehicle were struck by gunfire. Authorities released a photo of the recovered weapon, which Jaworski described as a short-barreled pistol. Julio Pitts, a resident in the area, said he was sitting in his living room when the shots rang out.

Authorities believe the shootout stemmed from an ongoing feud between the two teens. Jaworski said the incident appears to be isolated between the two juveniles with no threat to the community, but called it inherently dangerous because a car and house were hit. Neighbors said detectives were in the area throughout the night gathering evidence, and everyone is relieved no one was injured.
cards.article_text: Deputies with the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office are investigating a shootout between two teenagers, ages 15 and 17, in a residential neighborhood Wednesday night. Neighbors said detectives were in the area throughout the night gathering evidence, and everyone is relieved no one was injured. Julio Pitts, a resident in the area, said he was sitting in his living room when the shots rang out. "The car had to have been here, and he had to shoot like that, boom, boom, boom, boom," Pitts said. Authorities released a photo of one of the weapons believed to have been used in the shooting. Kevin Jaworski said the weapon was recovered after the 17-year-old suspect was taken into custody Thursday morning. "So, my first thing that comes to my mind is, where did he get it? This is a short-barreled pistol, a rifle that he was shooting in the middle of the street," Jaworski said. The incident occurred in the 1100 block of 12th Court Southwest at around 7:30 p.m. Deputies responded to multiple 911 calls and found bullet casings at the scene. A nearby home and vehicle had been struck by gunfire. Investigators said they obtained video showing the two teenagers shooting at each other in the roadway. "Yes, yes, between the 17-year-old and the 15-year-old, they were actively shooting at each other in the middle of the street," Jaworski said. Authorities believe the shootout stemmed from an ongoing feud between the two teens. While the cause of the feud remains unclear, officials said the incident appears to be isolated. "This was between those two juveniles, so there’s no threat to the community at this point, but it is inherently dangerous to be shooting firearms in the middle of the street because, like I said, a car was hit, a house was hit, and if anybody was in those, they could have very well easily been hurt," Jaworski said. Pitts expressed frustration over the incident and called for action to prevent similar events in the future. "I say crime watch, but when everybody sees something wrong, they got to say something," Pitts said. The case remains under investigation, and authorities are urging anyone with information to contact detectives. hero.headline: Vero Beach arrest prompts experts to warn parents about AI photo manipulation risk
hero.body:
A Vero Beach man faces charges for allegedly using artificial intelligence to turn social media photos into pornography, prompting child-safety experts to warn local parents about the growing threat of AI-generated exploitative images. Peter Ruma is accused of altering photos of one woman, and police believe there may be more victims with additional charges to follow. Greg Schiller, CEO of the Boca Raton-based nonprofit Child Rescue Coalition, said this type of activity is becoming increasingly common and that predators can use a simple photo of a child to create harmful content.

Schiller said the increased number of cyber tips related to AI-generated child sexual abuse material has gone through the roof. While Ruma's case does not involve children, Schiller said the accusations serve as a reminder that a photo posted on social media today could be altered into pornography by tomorrow. The Child Rescue Coalition provides technology to help law enforcement track down child sex predators worldwide.

Schiller advised parents and social media users to think carefully before posting pictures, especially of children. He said the easiest way to protect yourself and your family is to stop posting on social media, but acknowledged there are ways to continue posting while maintaining as much security as possible. Schiller recommended keeping social media settings private and limiting who can see your posts.

Schiller emphasized that nothing is truly safe on the internet. He said people need to be conscious of what others can potentially do with their images and understand there might be repercussions before acting. Ruma is currently charged with altering photos of one woman.

hero.headline: Vero Beach police expect more charges, additional victims in AI sexual image case against Peter Ruma
hero.body:
Vero Beach police said Thursday they believe there are additional victims and expect more charges against a man accused of creating and sharing AI-generated sexually explicit images of women without their consent. Police Chief David Currey said the current eight charges against 37-year-old Peter Solomon Ruma involve one adult female victim. Ruma is being held at the Indian River County Jail on $1 million bond.

Ruma is charged with three counts of creating an altered sexual depiction, three counts of promoting an altered sexual depiction, one count of sexual cyber harassment and one count of cyberstalking. Currey said investigators have identified several other women who may have been subjected to similar conduct, some of whom may not know their images were obtained, manipulated or shared. The investigation uncovered complaints and law enforcement contacts involving unwanted communications and similar behavior dating back several years.

Investigators said the victim came forward after discovering her image had been altered. Detectives searched Ruma's home and seized two phones, and a forensic review of the devices produced evidence that advanced the investigation. Police said Ruma allegedly used photographs of real women including images from social media and other publicly available online sources to make the altered sexual images. A person does not have to have sent an intimate photo to be victimized, police said.

Ruma is employed as a Lyft driver and Uber Eats driver. Currey stressed that investigators have not alleged criminal conduct occurred while Ruma was working for either service, but released the information as they seek potential victims or people with concerning interactions involving him. Police believe Ruma acted alone, though Currey said that could change as the investigation continues. Anyone who believes they may have been victimized, received altered or sexually explicit images from Ruma, or has information for detectives is asked to contact Vero Beach police Detective Greg Matakaitis at 772-978-4665.

hero.body:

Police said Peter Ruma downloaded pictures from social media and used AI prompts to digitally remove women's clothing and place them in sexual situations, then distributed the images. Authorities are warning there could be more victims.

Police said Ruma has been engaging in this activity for several years. He downloaded photographs of women from social media platforms and used artificial intelligence technology to manipulate the images by removing clothing and creating sexual scenarios. The manipulated images were then distributed without the consent of the individuals depicted.

Ruma is currently being held in the Indian River County Jail. The $1 million bond reflects the severity of the charges against him. Police said they are expected to provide an update this afternoon.

Authorities are warning that additional victims may exist. Police are encouraging anyone who believes they may have been victimized to come forward. The investigation remains active as officials work to identify the full scope of the alleged scheme.

hero.headline: Body found in Martin County mangroves believed to be missing Port St. Lucie man Michael Debevec
hero.body:
A body discovered deep within the mangroves near the House of Refuge in Martin County is believed to be that of Michael Anthony Debevec, a Port St. Lucie man reported missing in August. Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek announced Tuesday that investigators recovered the body after an extensive search, but decomposition prevented officials from confirming the cause of death. The deceased person was wearing clothing matching what Debevec was believed to have been wearing. Debevec's family was notified that a body was found, though official identification was still pending.

The search began Saturday after a Good Samaritan found a wallet belonging to Debevec and went to his home to return it, prompting his family to file a missing person report. Investigators found Debevec's vehicle Saturday afternoon at Chastain Beach, a little more than two miles from where the body was discovered. Detectives and ground and aerial units launched an extensive search following the discovery of the wallet and vehicle.

Investigators determined that Debevec traveled from the Port St. Lucie area to Martin County at about 3 a.m. on the 27th and parked at Chastain Beach. Phone records showed that his phone was in use Friday morning and moving back and forth between Chastain Beach and the House of Refuge. On Tuesday morning, investigators found a backpack belonging to Debevec hanging high in a tree with his computer inside.

A deeper search into the mangroves led investigators to the body. Budensiek said investigators had not officially confirmed whether the body was Debevec's. "So we do believe we found Mr. Unfortunately, there's a lot of decomposition that's taken place so it's really impossible to determine cause of death. What are we dealing with here? I don't know?" Budensiek said during a news conference Tuesday.

hero.headline: Palm City woman accused in Border Collie hoarding case posts bond, released from jail
hero.body:
The Palm City woman facing charges in a Border Collie hoarding investigation posted a $500 surety bond and was released from jail on Monday, according to Martin County court documents. Paige O'Donnell, 62, is facing 72 charges: 36 third-degree felony counts involving alleged animal cruelty and 36 misdemeanor counts alleging animals were kept without sufficient exercise and air.

The charges stem from last month when 36 Border Collies were recovered from O'Donnell's Palm City home in deplorable conditions. O'Donnell, a former dog breeder, was at the center of the investigation after authorities found the dogs at her residence.

The dogs have since been legally surrendered to the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast, and adoption applications opened on Tuesday. O'Donnell's attorney filed a waiver of appearance for her at the pre-trial hearings and entered a plea of not guilty to the charges.

No future court dates are currently listed in the case, according to court records.

hero.headline: Former DeSantis spokesperson's PR firm awarded more than $700K in state contracts, drawing watchdog scrutiny
hero.body:
A public relations firm owned by a former spokesperson for Governor Ron DeSantis has been awarded more than $700,000 in state government contracts across multiple Florida agencies over the past three years, raising questions from a nonpartisan watchdog group about whether political loyalty influenced the awards. State records show that TMF Communications, owned by Taryn Fenske, has secured five- and six-figure contracts for PR consulting work from several agencies since 2023, including the Department of Health, the Department of Children and Families, the Agency for Persons with Disabilities, New College, and the Justice Administration Commission. Fenske, a former GOP communications director who worked for DeSantis' executive communications team and later his presidential super PAC, launched the private firm after DeSantis' presidential run ended.

The contracts include nearly $40,000 from the Department of Health earlier this year, $113,000 from DCF in 2025 to support digital media vendors, $75,000 from the Agency for Persons with Disabilities in 2025 for rebranding work, another $52,000 allocation in 2026, more than $400,000 from New College since 2023 for PR consulting, and nearly $27,000 from the Justice Administration Commission in 2023 to assist with public relations after DeSantis suspended Orange County State Attorney Monique Worrell. Fenske built her political career in Tallahassee working for former Governor Rick Scott, the Republican National Committee, and Education Commissioner Richard Corcoran before joining the DeSantis administration.

Ben Wilcox, who leads Integrity Florida, a nonpartisan government watchdog group, criticized the arrangement after reviewing the contract records. "I think to the average citizen, the average taxpayer, that that's an exorbitant amount of money," Wilcox said. "I think it looks bad to the public. I think it looks like this communications consultant is being rewarded for her service to the DeSantis administration and to Governor DeSantis personally."

Fenske declined to speak on camera but called the premise that her loyalty to the DeSantis administration contributed to her state work "insulting and dismissive" of her professional qualifications in an email. She said her company's work was "earned on its merits." Alex Lanfranconi, DeSantis' current communications director, called TMF's state business "awesome" and described Fenske as "one of the best communications professionals in the state." DCF defended its contract with Fenske and noted that TMF appears on a list of state-approved PR vendors as neither the least nor the most expensive option.

hero.headline: Vero Beach man jailed on $1 million bond accused of using AI to create fake sexual images
hero.body:
A Vero Beach man is being held on $1 million bond after police said he used artificial intelligence to create and distribute fake sexual images of women for several years. Peter Ruma was arrested on charges including three counts of creation of an altered sexual depiction of an identifiable person, three counts of promotion of an altered sexual depiction, sexual cyberharassment, and stalking.

Vero Beach Police Department detectives said Ruma downloaded photographs from social media and other online sources, then used AI prompts to remove women's clothing and place them in sexual situations. He then distributed the altered images without the consent of the individuals depicted. Detectives executed search warrants on Ruma's residence and electronic devices, and a forensic examination recovered evidence investigators believe is associated with the creation and distribution of altered sexual images.

The current charges stem from incidents occurring between June and August 2026 and relate to one female victim. During the investigation, detectives identified several additional females believed to have been victimized through similar conduct. Investigators also have information indicating Ruma may have engaged in this type of conduct for several years.

Ruma is currently being held at the Indian River County Jail. hero.headline: Stuart judge rules man incompetent to stand trial in fatal stabbing of 73-year-old woman
hero.body:
A Martin County judge ruled that Kersten Francilus, 25, is incompetent to stand trial in the fatal stabbing of Joyce Ellen Thompson Adams, 73, in the Southwood community near Stuart. Two doctors examined Francilus and determined he is incompetent during a hearing on Aug. He has been remanded to a state mental hospital for restoration to competency before his case can proceed.

Francilus faces premeditated first-degree murder charges in the April 2025 attack at the intersection of Southeast Black Oak Lane and Woods Edge Trail. According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office arrest affidavit, the first responding deputy witnessed Francilus stabbing Adams in the neck and back. Investigators now believe she was stabbed more than 50 times. Francilus dropped the knife and complied with commands to get on the ground when ordered by deputies at gunpoint. First responders transported Adams to the Cleveland Clinic South Emergency Room, where she was pronounced dead.

Before the fatal stabbing, multiple residents reported a man matching Francilus' description walking through the Southwood neighborhood, approaching homes and asking about a nearby bank. One resident told investigators the man came to her house asking for a bank, and when she opened the door, he attempted to step inside. She shut the door and alerted her husband. Sheriff John Budensiek said Francilus specifically targeted women, asking whether their husbands were home, and approached two children in an open garage. Investigators spoke with Francilus' mother, who confirmed the serrated knife used in the attack came from their home. She told detectives she usually stored the knives above the microwave to hide them from her son. The mother also revealed her son had not taken his prescribed medication since February 2025.

The Martin County Sheriff's Office said Francilus had two prior encounters with law enforcement in 2025. One involved the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office and resulted in Francilus being Baker Acted. In September 2025, Francilus' mother called the Martin County Sheriff's Office to report her son was hearing voices. During an interview with investigators, Francilus admitted to leaving his residence and said he did what he did. When asked to describe Adams, Francilus said she was Jewish. Investigators spoke with Adams' daughter, who confirmed her mother was not Jewish. Budensiek said nothing currently indicates Francilus was antisemitic, but detectives are working to determine whether that belief played a role in why Adams was targeted.

cards.headline: Palm City Border Collie hoarding suspect released from jail on $500 bond
cards.teaser: Paige ODonnell, 62, posted bond and was released Monday after 36 Border Collies were recovered from her home in deplorable conditions last month.
cards.body:
The Palm City woman behind the Border Collie hoarding investigation posted a $500 surety bond and was released from jail on Monday, according to Martin County court documents. Paige ODonnell, 62, is facing 72 charges: 36 third-degree felony counts involving alleged animal cruelty and 36 misdemeanor counts alleging animals were kept without sufficient exercise and air.

Last month, ODonnell, a former dog breeder, was at the center of attention after 36 Border Collies were recovered from her Palm City home in deplorable conditions. The dogs have since been legally surrendered to the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast, and adoption applications opened on Tuesday.

ODonnells attorney filed a waiver of appearance for her at the pre-trial hearings and entered a plea of not guilty to the charges. No future court dates are listed.

hero.headline: DeSantis pledges to campaign for Amendment 3 despite growing local opposition over service cuts
hero.body:
Governor Ron DeSantis said Monday he will help persuade Floridians to approve Amendment 3, a property-tax proposal that would increase the homestead exemption for non-school property taxes to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, as the measure faces growing opposition from local leaders who warn the savings could force service cuts and higher fees. DeSantis said he plans to get involved in the campaign even though the amendment falls short of the broader tax relief he originally sought, though he has not settled on how he will participate and said he would not lead a political committee's statewide fundraising effort. The amendment would also lower the annual cap on assessment increases for non-homestead properties from 10% to 5% and restrict how counties and municipalities use property-tax revenue.

Miami-Dade County Mayor Daniella Levine Cava launched a South Florida campaign Wednesday to defeat Amendment 3, joined by local leaders, labor organizations and business and civic groups. Levine Cava warned that Miami-Dade could lose about 10% of its general fund revenue in the first year and 20% in the second, forcing difficult decisions about staffing and services. She said communities could face service cuts, higher fees or some combination of both, with renters and businesses potentially shouldering additional costs without receiving the expanded homestead exemption. DeSantis rejected warnings that the amendment would leave communities unable to provide basic services, saying homeowners need financial breathing room and local governments can adjust after years of growing property-tax collections.

A Sachs Media survey conducted Aug. 18 randomly assigned 800 Florida voters to groups reviewing either the original ballot language or a court-ordered revision. Support was 65% among those who read the revised wording, compared with 60% among those who saw the original, though the difference was not statistically significant. The Florida Policy Institute estimates that public hospital districts and health systems would lose approximately $323 million over three years under Amendment 3, with reduced funding potentially affecting staffing, access to care and programs serving uninsured and underinsured patients.

Amendment 3 requires approval from at least 60% of voters casting ballots on the measure in November. DeSantis said he would support state funding to help rural counties with limited tax bases absorb revenue losses, though any state assistance would depend on lawmakers approving the funding. Former Republican state Sen. Jeff Brandes wrote in a Florida Politics op-ed that losses in property-tax revenue could push rural counties to reconsider their resistance to data center projects as communities seek replacement revenue.
